name: Character Creation
content:
The characters you create in Renaissance will be stepping into a world that is experiencing a period of change and discovery. Peoples and traditions long isolated are colliding and mixing. Innovation and diversity are omnipresent. Through the choices you make in building your character, you will determine their place in this world by choosing:

  • Their ANCESTRY, which represents their genetic heritage.

  • Their CULTURE, which represents their lived experience.

  • Their MESTIERE, or adventuring discipline.

The countless combinations made possible by these sets of choices are intended as a mechanical reflection of a diverse world. There is no “right” or “wrong” way to build a character.

While certain combinations of choices may be more likely to produce successful dice rolls, know that character advancement is achieved exclusively through failures and overcoming hardship (see Character Advancement). A character that begins strong may learn and grow at a slower rate, while an initially weak character is more likely to advance quickly. Similarly, as the game progresses, a character who chooses to confront their weaknesses is more likely to learn from them and grow.

To build your character, follow the steps below. It is not required that you follow them in this exact sequence, but it may make the process a bit easier. The choices in each step bear influence on the choices made in all the other steps, so if you get to a point in the process where a decision made earlier no longer fits the character concept, it is totally ok to go back and change your decisions (although you may not redo dice rolls or coin flips unless your GM allows it).

1) CHOOSE YOUR ANCESTRY

The Recent Upheaval (see Campaign Creation) served as a great “stirring of the pot.” As it affected each part of the campaign world, it spurred populations to move into unfamiliar areas. While many places still bear the strong influence of the peoples that founded them, their populations are now richly diverse. As a result, the offspring of these diverse places often draw their heritage from more than one Ancestry.

Your character’s Ancestry represents the influence of genetics and anatomy on their abilities:

GENETIC HERITAGE

Review the Ancestries catalog. You may choose one or two Ancestries for your character. If you choose one Ancestry, you get all the Abilities of that Ancestry. If you choose two Ancestries, follow these steps to determine your unique genetic makeup:

  1. Make a grid with two columns. Assign one Ancestry to each column.

  2. Put the first Ability listed for each Ancestry in the first row.

  3. Continue adding rows, with one Ability per row, until all Abilities for both Ancestries are listed. If one Ancestry has more Abilities than the other, leave the opposite side of the row blank.

  4. Assign each Ancestry heads or tails. Moving top to bottom, flip a coin for each pair of Abilities to determine which Ability your character receives. For rows where both sides have an Ability, you receive whichever Ability the coin indicates. For rows where one side is blank, you either receive the Ability on the non-blank side or nothing, depending on the coin result.

  5. Combine the results into your unique set of Ancestry Abilities.

Because Ancestries each have a minimum of two Abilities, a dual-Ancestry character will always end up with at least two Ancestry Abilities.

Add your Ancestry and Ancestry Abilities to your character sheet.

SPEED, HEIGHT, WEIGHT, AGE

Each Ancestry defines your character’s SPEED (in feet), as well as common ranges for HEIGHT, WEIGHT and AGE. Choose where your character falls in those ranges. If your character is of dual Ancestry, use the lowest minimum and highest maximum among the two Ancestries as a range for each attribute. Record these values on your character sheet.

2) CHOOSE YOUR CULTURE(S)

In this world of change, discovery and migration, it’s not uncommon to be born in one place and to come of age in another. The places you’ve lived help tell the story of who you are.

LIVED EXPERIENCE

Review the Cultures catalog. You may choose one or two Cultures. If you choose one Culture, you get all the abilities of that Culture. If you choose two Cultures, choose one Ability from each Culture. Either way, when considering your choices, think about what part of your character’s life has impressed each benefit upon them.

Add your Culture(s) and Culture Abilities to your character sheet.

3) DETERMINE YOUR CORE STATS

Now that you know a bit about where your character comes from, fill out the main section of your character sheet.

CORE STATS

To determine your character’s initial Core Stats (see Core Stats), roll 5d4 and drop the highest and lowest results. Assign each of the three remaining die results to one of your Core Stats: BODY, HEART and WITS.

INITIAL SKILL RANKS

For each point assigned to a Core Stat, you may take one rank in a Skill under that Core Stat's domain - in the column below it.

For example, a score of 3 in BODY would allow you to take 1 rank each in 3 skills, 2 ranks in 1 skill and 1 rank in another, or 3 ranks in 1 skill - all in the column under BODY.

You will have the opportunity to increase these scores and ranks as your character gains experience.

VIRTUES

Calculate the maximums for your Virtues:

  • Your maximum Endurance is equal to 5 times your BODY score.

  • Your maximum Hope is equal to 2 times your HEART score.

  • Your maximum Defense is equal to 10 plus your WITS score.

Each Virtue starts with a current score equal to its maximum.

WEAKNESSES, STATES & CONDITIONS

All Weaknesses start with a score of 0 by default. All States and Conditions are unchecked by default.

4) CHOOSE YOUR MESTIERE

Your MESTIERE ("may-stee-AIR-ay" - literally "Mastery") is your adventuring discipline: the special set of skills that you bring to the Questing life.

Your character has attained Novizio ("no-VEE-tzee-oh" - literally "Novice") status within one Mestiere. Review the Mestieri catalog and choose one.

When you choose a Mestiere, you gain its Novizio Abilities at no cost. These are the foundation of the Mestiere's system of Abilities and define the basic toolkit of the discipline — including how the Mestiere generates or manages Mestiere Points, if applicable (see Abilities). If there is more than one set of Novizio abilities within the Mestiere, choose one.

Add the Novizio Abilities to your character sheet and adjust your base Mestieri Points as defined by the Mestiere. Also note the Mestiere's Martial Training, adding any Engagement Dice and Engagement Successes it provides to your character sheet.

As your character gains experience through gameplay, you will have the opportunity to buy additional Abilities within your Mestiere of choice.

Each Mestiere offers a unique approach to the game. Some express that approach solely through core game mechanics like Martial Training and Abilities. Others introduce mechanics that are entirely unique to that Mestiere: decks of cards with predictive powers, collections of summonable beasts, interactions with the natural environment, systems for tracking spiritual balance, even methods for writing your own spells. Find a Mestiere that resonates with the character concept you've developed and with the game experience you want to have.

Note that there is not an option to dip into another Mestiere later on, so this is a big, permanent decision. Your choice of Mestiere will define the majority of your character's mechanical interactions with the campaign world.

5) DETERMINE INITIAL KEEPING & TREASURE

Roll a d4 to determine your starting KEEPING tier: a result of 1 means Modest, 2 means Comfortable, 3 means Prosperous, and 4 means Opulent (see Treasure & Keeping). You may choose to start Wretched if you feel that makes narrative sense for your character, but know that you'll be unable to purchase any starting Equipment.

Once your starting Keeping is determined, roll a number of d20 equal to that Keeping's cost: 1d20 for Modest, 2d20 for Comfortable, 3d20 for Prosperous, 4d20 for Opulent. The total is your starting Treasure.

You may spend as much or as little of this Treasure as you like on Equipment items from your Culture(s) of origin before beginning play. Add the Equipment items to your character sheet and subtract their cost from your starting Treasure. Be sure to add any Engagement Dice or Engagement Successes it provides to your character sheet.

Any unspent Treasure carries forward with you into the campaign.

5) NAME & FINISHING TOUCHES

Now that your character sheet is mostly filled out, it's time to pick a name, pronouns and think up a bit of backstory.

Look at the choices you've made as you've built this character and ask: How did their genetic heritage define where they started? How did their time among the Culture(s) they grew up in shape them? What has spurred them to pursue the Questing life now? Where are they heading? What are they looking for? What do they fear? What do they want?

Mull these questions and put down some details to start with, but leave space within your answers. Discovering the character through the game is half the fun. You're a new character in Renaissance you're about to make a lot of mistakes and learn quickly from them. The journey begins here!
